title: Set 284

sentences.ko: 그거 말고. 그거 벌써 두 번이나 틀었는데 너 두 번 다 잠들었잖아. 오늘 밤에 뭐 틀 거면 네가 진짜 안 자고 끝까지 볼 만한 걸로 해야 돼.
sentences.text: Not that one, we already started it twice and you fell asleep both times. If we're putting something on tonight, it has to be something you'll actually stay awake for.

alts.text: Nah, not that one. We've tried it twice and you conked out both times. If we're watching something tonight, it's gotta be something you'll actually stay up for.

I would prefer not to watch that one. We have already started it twice, and you fell asleep on both occasions. If we are going to watch something this evening, it should be something you will actually stay awake for.

sentences.note: **putting something on** 은 영화나 프로그램을 틀다라는 뜻입니다. **stay awake for** 는 ~을 보는 동안 깨어 있다이고, 캐주얼의 **conked out** 은 곯아떨어졌다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 회사 근처 샌드위치 가게 또 가격 올린 거 봤어? 똑같은 샌드위치가 이제 14달러쯤 해. 그래서 도시락 싸 오기 시작했어. 진짜 싫은데 매일 그 돈을 낼 수는 없잖아.
sentences.text: Did you see the sandwich place by work raised their prices again? It's like fourteen bucks now for the same sandwich, so I've started bringing my own lunch, which I hate, but I can't keep paying that every day.

alts.text: Ugh, you hear the sandwich place by work jacked up their prices again? It's like fourteen bucks now for the exact same sandwich. So I'm bringing my own lunch now. I hate it, but I can't keep paying that every day.

Have you noticed that the sandwich shop near my office has raised its prices again? It is now about fourteen dollars for the same sandwich, so I have begun bringing my own lunch. I do not enjoy it, but I cannot continue paying that amount every day.

sentences.note: **raised their prices** 는 가격을 올렸다이고, 캐주얼의 **jacked up** 은 확 올렸다는 느낌입니다. **bucks** 는 달러를 편하게 부르는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 걔 진짜 웃기거든. 근데 낯을 좀 가려서 처음에 좀 진지해 보여도 한 20분만 기다려 봐. 그리고 일 얘기는 꺼내지 마. 얼마 전에 회사에서 잘려서 아직 많이 속상해하거든.
sentences.text: So she's really funny, but it takes her a while to warm up, so if she seems kind of serious at first, just give it like twenty minutes. And don't ask about her job, because she just got laid off and she's still pretty upset about it.

alts.text: Heads up, she's super funny, but she takes a while to warm up. If she seems kinda serious at first, just give it twenty minutes or so. Oh, and don't bring up her job. She just got laid off and she's still pretty upset.

She is genuinely very funny, but she takes some time to become comfortable with people, so if she appears rather serious at first, please allow about twenty minutes. Also, I would ask that you not inquire about her work, as she was recently laid off and remains quite upset about it.

sentences.note: **warm up** 은 사람이 낯선 자리에서 점점 편해지다, 마음을 열다라는 뜻입니다. **got laid off** 는 정리해고를 당했다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 친구 소개팅 주선하면서 상대가 어떤 사람인지 설명하기

sentences.ko: 그 기침 때문에 드디어 병원 가 봤는데, 알고 보니 그냥 안 떨어지는 감기였어. 대기실에서 한 시간이나 앉아 있다가 물 많이 마시라는 말만 들었어. 그래도 이제 걱정은 안 해도 되니까 다행이지.
sentences.text: I finally went in about that cough, and it turns out it's just a cold that wouldn't go away. So I sat in the waiting room for an hour just to be told to drink more water, but at least now I can stop worrying about it.

alts.text: Okay, I finally got that cough checked out. Turns out it's just a cold that won't quit. So I sat in the waiting room for an hour just to get told to drink more water, but hey, at least I can stop worrying now.

I finally saw a doctor about my cough, and it turns out it is simply a cold that has been lingering. I waited for an hour in the waiting room only to be advised to drink more water, but at least I no longer need to worry about it.

sentences.note: **went in about** 은 어떤 증상 때문에 병원에 가서 진찰을 받았다는 뜻입니다. **it turns out** 은 알고 보니라는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 병원 갔다 온 얘기 가볍게 하기

sentences.ko: 세상에, 진짜 오랜만이다! 마지막으로 들은 게 너 다시 학교 다닐까 고민 중이라는 거였는데, 그래서 결국 다녔어, 아니면 마음 바꿨어?
sentences.text: Oh my god, it's been forever! Last I heard you were thinking about going back to school, so did you end up doing it, or did you change your mind?

alts.text: No way, it's been ages! Last thing I heard, you were thinking about going back to school. So, did you do it or change your mind?
It has been such a long time! The last I heard, you were considering returning to school. Did you ultimately decide to do so, or did you change your mind?

sentences.note: **it's been forever** 는 정말 오랜만이다라는 말입니다. **end up** 은 결국 ~하게 되다라는 뜻으로, did you end up doing it 은 결국 했어?가 됩니다.

reviewed: 1번 note: 별표로 감싼 put something on 이 문장에 그대로 없어서 실제로 나오는 putting something on 으로 바꿈
4번 casual: 따옴표 없이 just to hear drink more water 라고 쓰면 읽을 때 헷갈려서 just to get told to drink more water 로 고침
5번 casual: or'd 는 글로 적으면 어색하고 실제로 잘 안 쓰는 줄임이라 So, did you do it or change your mind? 로 고침
